> What might be eating the acorns under our oak trees at night?
Likely nighttime acorn eaters include deer, raccoons, opossums, mice, rats, squirrels, chipmunks, and wild pigs, depending on your region. Look for tracks, droppings, rooting, or gnawed shells, or set up a motion-activated trail camera to identify the visitor.

> Would the same animals eat hazelnuts?
Yes—many of the same animals eat hazelnuts, especially squirrels, chipmunks, mice, rats, raccoons, deer, and wild pigs; opossums may eat kernels they can access. Rodents usually leave neatly gnawed shells, while deer and pigs may crush or swallow nuts and disturb the ground.
150 tokens in
> How could we find out which one it is?
Set an infrared motion-activated trail camera 30–60 cm (1–2 ft) above the ground, aimed at the nut fall area, and check footage over several nights. Also smooth a patch of damp soil or sand to capture tracks and note scat, rooting, and shell damage—paired chisel-like gnaw marks suggest rodents, while crushed nuts and churned soil suggest deer or wild pigs.
